content.text: Root cause:

Caused by: java.nio.file.FileAlreadyExistsException: /opt/fedora6
	at java.base/sun.nio.fs.UnixException.translateToIOException(UnixException.java:94)
	at java.base/sun.nio.fs.UnixException.rethrowAsIOException(UnixException.java:111)
	at java.base/sun.nio.fs.UnixException.rethrowAsIOException(UnixException.java:116)
	at java.base/sun.nio.fs.UnixFileSystemProvider.createDirectory(UnixFileSystemProvider.java:389)
	at java.base/java.nio.file.Files.createDirectory(Files.java:690)
	at java.base/java.nio.file.Files.createAndCheckIsDirectory(Files.java:797)
	at java.base/java.nio.file.Files.createDirectories(Files.java:743)
	at org.fcrepo.config.FedoraPropsConfig.postConstruct(FedoraPropsConfig.java:130)
This is quite funny because the method being called is Files.createDirectories(), and the javadoc claims:
> Creates a directory by creating all nonexistent parent directories first.
Unlike the createDirectory method, an exception
is not thrown if the directory could not be created because it already
exists.
https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.base/java/nio/file/Files.html#createDirectories(java.nio.file.Path,java.nio.file.attribute.FileAttribute...)
Upon further testing, the error is only thrown when the entire path points to a symlink, not when one of the parent directories in the path is a symlink.
Example that works:  /opt/fedora -> /home/projects/sprater/fedora;  fcrepo.home=/opt/fedora/fedora6
Example that fails:  /opt/fedora6 -> /home/projects/sprater/fedora/fedora6;  fcrepo.home=/opt/fedora6
The same issue occurs when fcrepo.ocfl.root is set to a path the ends in a symlink.  May be an issue for any property that is a path?
Unfortunately, it sounds like this is the intended behavior of the API:
https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8130464
We'll need to check if the path exists before calling Files.createDirectories
https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/pull/1904
Resolves:
https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/commit/29be448d57d7d4ddc6186ed3a3c6b55185b84063
When I attempt to run the fcrepo-webapp one-click application with fcrepo.home set to a path that is a symlink, the application cannot read the location and throws a
java.nio.file.FileAlreadyExistsException
.  If I change the location to the explicit path, the application starts up without a problem.
This is the symlink.  Note that /home and /opt are on different filesystems (though that shouldn't make a difference).  The symlink is soft.
lrwxrwxrwx. 1 root root 37 Feb 23 19:11 /opt/fedora6 -> /home/sprater/projects/fedora/fedora6
Here is a sample command line, with fcrepo.home pointed to the symlink:
java -Dfcrepo.home=/opt/fedora6 -Dfcrepo.ocfl.root=/opt/ocfl/data/ocfl-root -jar fcrepo-webapp/target/fcrepo-webapp-6.0.0-SNAPSHOT-jetty-console.jar
Attached is a log with the full output and stack trace when fcrepo.home points to a symlink.
CentOS 7, two filesystems of type xfs
